text.p: These are the leading stories in the Malawian press on Friday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- A full blown-up picture of a bespectacled smiling general manager for Agricultural Development and Marketing Corporation (ADMARC), Eunice Kazembe, covers the whole front page with a banner headline: Woman of the year 1996.

- Lands and Valuation Minister Peter Fachi said on Thursday that government will re-posses a 350-acre piece of land distributed to the ruling party's four top officials, Information minister, Brown Mpinganjira, Deputy finance minister Lizzy Lossa and two others to re-distribute it to the landless people in Mulanje, southern Malawi.

- The Civil Servants Trade Union said it would fight on for higher salaries and more non-salary benefits following government's announcement that it will give a pay increase to all civil servants this year.
Civil servants threatened a nation-wide strike on December 23 but goverment was quick to back down and announced it would implement recommendations for higher salaries.

- A Catholic backed revolutionist local grouping, Alleluya Band, advocating for the abolition of the death penalty, on December 30, staged a live performance at Zomba Central prison where death sentences are carried out, the first time in the history of Malawi that prisoners were entertained.
Malawi's parliament last year retained the death penalty in the constitution.

- The Public Affairs Committee, a body that mediates Malawi's transition process, said on Thursday it did not know of any plans to mediate the stalled talks between the ruling United Democratic Front party and two opposition Malawi Congress Pary and the Alliance for Democracy scheduled for January 8.
